title: Jollof Sauce
author: Zoe Adjei
desc: A litre of sauce simmered thirty to forty minutes — closer to forty with tinned tomatoes, to cook out the acidity.
longDesc: The sauce the one-pot jollof is built on, and it is a separate preparation worth keeping. An onion is fried until translucent, half a tablespoon each of curry and chilli powder go in for two minutes, then ginger, garlic, an optional scotch bonnet, optional thyme, a heaped tablespoon of the jollof dry spice mix, tinned or fresh tomatoes, tomato purée, salt and stock. It is blended with a stick blender and simmered thirty to forty minutes — closer to forty if using tinned tomatoes, in order to cook out their acidity. It makes a litre and keeps three days chilled.
ingredients: Sunflower or other cooking oil — no quantity is printed
2.5 cm fresh root ginger, grated — unpeeled if organic
1 scotch bonnet chilli, deseeded and roughly chopped (optional)
1 heaped tbsp jollof dry spice mix (GHA101)
1 x 400 g tin tomatoes, or 250 g fresh tomatoes, diced
1 tsp sea salt, or to taste
100 ml good quality chicken or vegetable stock
steps: Add the curry powder and chilli powder and cook 2 minutes.
Add the ginger, garlic, scotch bonnet, thyme and the jollof dry spice mix.
Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, salt and stock.
Simmer over medium-low heat 30 to 40 minutes — closer to 40 minutes if using tinned tomatoes, in order to cook out the acidity of the tomatoes.
Cool and store, or use straight away.
chefTips: Forty minutes if you use tinned tomatoes, thirty if fresh. Her reasoning is explicit — the tinned need longer to cook out their acidity — and it is the kind of distinction most recipes skip.
Blend AFTER everything is in and BEFORE the long simmer. A stick blender in the pan is what she specifies.
The oil carries no quantity at all in the source. Two tablespoons for a litre of sauce is a reasonable reading, offered as such.
Twenty-five grams of thyme leaves is a very large amount of fresh thyme, and it is optional. Taste before committing to all of it.
Keeps up to three days chilled. Make a double batch if you are planning jollof, since the one-pot takes five hundred millilitres of it.
This is a different sauce from chalé sauce, which underpins her groundnut soups — chalé is a raw blended base, this is a cooked and spiced sauce.
An imperial printing of the same recipe gives a flat forty minutes rather than the thirty-to-forty range, so forty is the safer figure.
commonMistakes: Thirty minutes with tinned tomatoes, leaving it sharp.
All twenty-five grams of thyme without tasting.
Making only one batch when the jollof needs half a litre.
sources: Adapted from 'Jollof Sauce', taste.co.za. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'By Zoe Adjonyoh'. Date printed '07 February 2021'. CREDIT: 'extract from Zoe's Ghana Kitchen... published by Octopus Publishing Group'. Yield as printed: 'Makes 1 litre'. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS).

Ingredients exactly as printed: sunflower or other cooking oil — NO QUANTITY PRINTED; 1 large onion, finely sliced; ½ T curry powder; ½ T chilli powder; '2,5 cm fresh root ginger, grated (unpeeled if organic)' — the comma decimal is printed that way; 1 garlic clove, crushed; 1 Scotch Bonnet chilli, deseeded and roughly chopped (optional); 25 g thyme leaves, chopped (optional); 1 heaped T Jollof dry spice mix; 1 x 400g tin tomatoes or 250 g fresh tomatoes diced; 1 heaped T tomato purée; 1 t sea salt or to taste; 100 ml good quality chicken or vegetable stock.

A MISSING QUANTITY, flagged: the OIL has no amount printed, which is unusual in an otherwise fully quantified recipe. No figure is asserted; the two tablespoons in the tips is explicitly labelled a reading.

Method as printed: fry the onion 'until translucent', then the powders 2 minutes; add aromatics, tomatoes, purée, salt and stock; blend with a stick blender. THE CUE, verbatim: 'Simmer over a medium-low heat for 30-40 minutes (closer to 40 minutes if using tinned tomatoes in order to cook out the acidity of the tomatoes).' Keeps up to 3 days chilled.

A SECOND PRINTING, SINGLE-PASS: oprah.com's version of the same recipe shows imperial equivalents — '1 3/4 pints', '1 oz. thyme', '3 1/2 oz. chicken or vegetable stock' — and says flatly 'Simmer 40 minutes' rather than giving a range. Its credit is 'Zoe Adjonyoh from Zoe's Ghana Kitchen (Octopus Books, 2017)'. NOTE that 1 oz is about 28 g, which corroborates the 25 g of thyme.

THIS SAUCE IS NOT CHALÉ SAUCE, and the distinction matters because this author uses both. Chalé sauce (GHA031, GHA032) is a raw blended tomato-and-pepper base, measured by volume into other dishes and optionally cooked. Jollof sauce is cooked, spiced with her dry spice mix, and blended smooth. They are separate products in her repertoire.
IT DEPENDS ON the jollof dry spice mix at GHA101, which has two printings that disagree substantially — so a litre of this sauce will vary with which spice mix you made.
NO YIELD PER SERVING is printed; the eight servings above is an editorial division of a litre.
storage: Up to 3 days chilled, per the author. It freezes well.
reheating: Gentle heat. It thickens on standing.
healthBenefits: Cooked tomato is high in lycopene, more bioavailable with fat and heat.
Thyme, ginger and garlic all carry documented antimicrobial compounds.
Vegetarian with vegetable stock, and low in calories.
Capsaicin from the chilli powder and scotch bonnet.
culturalNote: Keeping a jollof sauce in the fridge is the move that makes a party dish into a weeknight one, and the distinction between thirty minutes for fresh tomatoes and forty for tinned is the sort of detail that only emerges when someone cooks the same thing hundreds of times.
